source_evidence: Some variable life insurance policies require you to pay a set amount in premiums. Others allow you to pay varying premiums as long as you contribute enough to cover policy fees and expenses. The money in the account gets invested in a selection of investment options—typically mutual funds— that you can choose.
answer: With variable life insurance, premiums go into an account, but fees may be taken out first, so the full amount you pay may not be invested. Depending on the policy, premiums may be fixed or may vary, provided you pay enough to cover policy fees and expenses. The remaining account money is invested in options you select, typically mutual funds. The account’s value depends in part on how those investments perform.
